title: Status Review Calendar — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
Some tiers of **Hardship and Protective Holds** are reviewed at fixed intervals while they run. The calendar below gives, per tier, the interval between status reviews and the overdue period after a review falls due.

| Tier | Review interval (calendar days) | Review overdue days (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | 0 | 0 |
| Documented Hardship Hold | 0 | 0 |
| Disaster Relief Hold | 0 | 0 |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | 0 | 0 |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | 60 | 15 |
| Military Service Hold | 90 | 30 |

- **Review interval** — the calendar days between status reviews while the hold runs; 0 means no reviews.
- **Review overdue days** — the calendar days after a review falls due before an unreviewed hold ends; 0 where no reviews apply.

## Points of reading

- Only the Long-Term Hardship Hold and the Military Service Hold are reviewed. Every other tier shows an interval of 0, meaning no reviews.
- A Long-Term Hardship Hold is reviewed every 60 calendar days and has an overdue period of 15 calendar days; a Military Service Hold is reviewed every 90 calendar days and has an overdue period of 30 calendar days.
- A tier without reviews has no overdue period (0 days).

## Illustration (hypothetical)

Reviews of a Military Service Hold are spaced 90 calendar days apart. If a review falls due on 1 June, its overdue period of 30 calendar days runs through 1 July, and the next review falls due 90 calendar days after 1 June, on 30 August.
